mekki-muskil:1-1.t:
His saying, Exalted is He (برب الناس): the origin of (الناس), according to Sībawayh, is «أناس», and the alif and lām are a substitute for the hamza. Ibn al-Anbārī said: (الناس) is a plural that has no singular from its own wording, on a par with «الإبل» (camels), «الخيل» (horses), «النعم» (livestock), «البقر» (cattle), «الغزاة» (raiders) and «القضاة» (judges): these plurals have no singulars from their own wordings. He said: «الإنسان» is not the singular of (الناس), and «القاضي» is not the singular of «القضاة». He said: the measure of (الناس) in terms of the verb [pattern] is «فعل», and its origin is «نسي», from «نسيت» (I forgot); the ʿayn was put after and the lām before, so in status it became «نيس», and the yāʾ became an alif because it was vowelled and what preceded it had fatḥa. He said: some grammarians said: the origin of (الناس) is «الأناس»; the hamza was lightened, and a nūn was substituted for the quiescent lām of definiteness and assimilated into the nūn after it, so it became a doubled nūn, as Allah said (لكنا هو الله ربي), meaning «لكن أنا». He said: al-Farrāʾ invalidates this answer, saying: we found the Arabs saying in its diminutive «نويس». Al-Farrāʾ said: had what they said been correct, the diminutive would be «أنيس» and «أنيس». [Translator's note: the two forms are printed identically in the source; presumably two different vocalisations were intended.]
His saying (ملك) and (إله): a badal (substitute) for (رب) or a naʿt (adjective) of it. His saying (من الجنة والناس): (الناس) is genitive (khafḍ), conjoined to (الوسواس), i.e. from the evil of the whisperer and of the people. It is not permissible to conjoin it to (الجنة), because people do not whisper in the breasts of people; only the jinn whisper. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «لا يوسوسون في صدور والناس», evidently corrupt; rendered according to its evident sense.] So since the meaning [otherwise] is impossible, you take it as conjoined to (الوسواس).
The book is complete, by the praise of Allah and His favour; and may Allah bless our master Muhammad and his family and companions and grant them peace.
